title: References of the land
preface: A tale refers. These are the rooms, creatures, objects, and rumours it points at without stopping for.

inWhich.1: a dog finds an egg the maps will not admit
inWhich.2: the grove answers a beat late, and will not swear to it
inWhich.3: two roads claim the same step
inWhich.4: keys are filed smaller, and none of them fit
inWhich.5: two slips try to be one harvest
inWhich.6: glass shows a light it does not own
inWhich.7: an oath is paid in fruit
inWhich.8: water keeps a face without stealing it
inWhich.9: the ninth honk is missing, and warms
inWhich.10: a hall tells the truth with its weight
inWhich.11: a garden blooms before its seed arrives
inWhich.12: rivers meet and remember their names
inWhich.13: the last door is shaped like a shell, and stays open

entries.title: The unnamed egg
entries.note: Warm where it ought to have been cold. No nest. No mother. The maps will not write it down. Carry it if you must; naming it is a kind of debt.

track.lanes: Warm where it ought to have been cold, they say in the margins; no nest, no mother, and the maps will not write it down.

after.says: Warm where it ought to have been cold. No nest. No mother. The maps will not write it down. Somebody carrying a pie has passed something warm like it {{n}} time{{s}}, and each time the pie settled. Carry it if you must; naming it is a kind of debt.

entries.title: Boof
entries.note: A dog. She works for the land, not for pay. She trusts a scent that ends in something real, and is suspicious of applause.

entries.title: Boonberries
entries.note: Ordinary magic: fruit, lantern-fuel, seed, and supper. Now and then one of them notices the story it is sitting in, which is more than most fruit will do.

track.lanes: Now and then a boonberry notices the story it is sitting in, they say in the margins, which is more than most fruit will do.

after.says: Ordinary magic: fruit, lantern-fuel, seed, and supper. Somebody carrying a pie has eaten {{n}} in passing and seen the clear way a breath before they needed it; whether the berry showed it or they remembered it, nobody can say.

entries.title: The Commons Scale
entries.note: Where the harvest is counted in public. A scale that belongs to the commons, not to a landlord. Intact seals have been known to lie.

entries.title: The maps that look away
entries.note: Boon.land's records hold only what the world has agreed exists. Ink that beads and will not take is not a metaphor. It is a refusal.

entries.title: The Grove of Echoes
entries.note: A thicket that replays testimony. Workers will not name it after dark. An echo is a summons, not evidence, which has disappointed several clerks.

entries.title: Crosswind Council
entries.note: Boon and bane sit under one weather. Keys may be filed smaller. They may not be grown while the room is asleep.

entries.title: A slip
entries.note: The paper a turn leaves behind. Two slips for one harvest cannot both post. A false slip is refused, which is how you know the walk means it.

entries.title: Lantern glass
entries.note: Bonk City's lanterns show light. They are not the light. Confusing the pane with the flame has started several small fires, all of them rhetorical.

track.lanes: Every pane here was once a blow, they say in the margins. The kiln melts the hurt out and pours it off clear.

after.says: Bonk City's lanterns show light. They are not the light. Somebody carrying a pie has struck {{n}} pane{{s}} in the lanes, and the kiln has taken every one back without asking whose. Put a palm to the glass and they are in there with the rest.

entries.title: The market stone
entries.note: An oath is public. The fruit is private. The egg, if present, is the witness, and does not sign.

entries.title: The Watering Eye
entries.note: A well that folds a face without stealing it. Water keeps what you put in. It will not call it yours.

entries.title: A dam, worded exactly
entries.note: Two beavers took a whole evening over a dam and went out to build it before anyone could quote a price. Below it the water comes to the well slow and clear.

track.lanes: Two beavers took a whole evening over one dam, they say in the margins, and finished it themselves.

after.says: Two beavers took a whole evening over a dam and went out to build it before anyone could quote a price. Somebody carrying a pie has been lent their pace {{n}} time{{s}} since, and the water below the dam is in no more of a hurry for it. Whose dam? They would want that worded exactly.

entries.title: The ninth honk
entries.note: Eight were sounded. The ninth was not. Its shard, if you believe the ridge, is warm and egg-shaped. No single keeper can hold the whole call.

entries.title: Bone.land
entries.note: The chassis. Joints exposed on purpose. A hall that would rather bonk you than flatter you. Plaster stories do not last here.

entries.title: The Boonberry Fool
entries.note: A spirit of wonder who keeps the town from growing too tidy. Often upside down. Rarely helpful in the way one hopes.

entries.title: A cell keeps its own law
entries.note: What remains the same under every honest test. The egg is one. The maps are not its jurisdiction.

entries.title: A key files smaller
entries.note: Permission may be narrowed. It may not be secretly widened. Brass that grows teeth overnight is a crime and a joke.

entries.title: A turn is admitted, or not
entries.note: Two routes that want the same next step must post as one. The sand is particular about this.

entries.title: The Scriptorium
entries.note: Where chambers are seeded, revised, and set on a calendar of stones. Patron seals buy presence, not rewrite rights.

entries.title: Lines in the sand
entries.note: Near the signal stones someone has drawn a circle over a rectangle, with four straight lines for limbs. Above it, a hat — drawn, but not touching.

entries.title: Three records of one visitor
entries.note: The council keeps three entries for a guest nobody invited: a pupil, a parcel, a door. The clerks have compared them. All three are correct.

entries.title: A hat, first
entries.note: Lamplighters report a bowler hat above the crowd on the glass bridge, moving against the traffic. Nobody reports a face. Everybody reports the hat.

entries.title: A puzzle with corners
entries.note: Laid out on the ridge, the shards fit best where they make right angles. Nobody set them that way. The honks came out square.

entries.title: Facing another way
entries.note: In the bloom every head turned toward the throne. One small figure at the back faced ninety degrees away, toward the garden wall, as if the story were over there.

entries.title: A true scent
entries.note: At the confluence Boof stops, nose up, at an empty place on the bridge rail. The map shows no one there. She waits the way she waits for someone she knows.

entries.title: The ant hearths
entries.note: Under the berry rows, small streets no map has room for. The ants keep torches along the roots and hold the winter off with other cold-blooded neighbours. They have never asked anyone for anything.

entries.title: A glassed folio
entries.note: A page pressed under a sheet of Bonk glass. It stops taking ink and starts keeping it, weather or no weather. When the story changes you glass a new page over the old; the older lines stay legible underneath. Anyone can make one. The round room's last page has never been glassed.

entries.title: Clowns, going home
entries.note: All evening, at the edge of the plaza, clowns went home with pie on their faces, delighted. Nobody at the table saw where the pie had come from. The pie on the table was no smaller.

track.lanes: Clowns go home delighted from the plaza's edge, they say, and nobody at the table sees where the pie came from.

after.says: All evening, at the edge of the plaza, clowns went home with pie on their faces: {{n}} of them so far, from somebody's carries through here. Nobody at the table saw where the pie had come from. The pie on the table was no smaller.

entries.title: A notice with nothing on it
entries.note: Someone has pasted a placard to the garden wall with nothing written on it. Passers-by stop to agree with it, silently. One has drawn a pie on it, and crossed the pie out.

track.lanes: Someone pasted a placard with nothing on it to the garden wall; passers-by agreed with it, silently, and one drew a pie on it and crossed the pie out.

after.says: Someone has pasted a placard to the garden wall with nothing written on it. There are {{n}} more like it now, one in every chapter the mimes hold. Passers-by agree with them, silently; one has drawn a pie on each and crossed it out.

entries.title: Plates, after
entries.note: By the cold spring water someone has stacked the plates from a meal nobody here remembers eating. The stack is taller than the meal could have been. Nobody saw who washed them.

track.lanes: Plates are stacked by the cold spring water, taller than the meal could have been, and nobody saw who washed them.

after.says: By the cold spring water someone has stacked the plates from a meal nobody here remembers eating: {{n}} plate{{s}}, one for every pie that went into a delighted face. The stack is taller than the meal could have been. Nobody saw who washed them.

entries.title: Prints at right angles
entries.note: The frost on the field that kept the Thursday holds the prints of nobody: a step, a right angle, a step, straight across, the way no road goes.

track.lanes: The frost on the field holds the prints of nobody, they say: a step, a right angle, a step.

after.says: The frost on the field that kept the Thursday holds a second set of prints now, a lane apart and level, as if someone had carried something across it without spilling it: {{n}} time{{s}}. Nobody was in the day to see who.

entries.title: Foretellings, unsaid
entries.note: On the hill they say a baneberry tells you what will go wrong, and that it goes wrong because you were told. Nobody on the hill has ever heard of one that kept quiet.

track.lanes: On the hill they say a baneberry tells you what will go wrong, and that it goes wrong because you were told.

after.says: On the hill they say a baneberry tells you what will go wrong, and that it goes wrong because you were told. Lately some have kept quiet: {{n}} stepped on before they could say a thing, somewhere in the lanes, and nothing went wrong that day because of them.

entries.title: Priced against himself
entries.note: At the crack they say the Genie cannot pass three of a thing without pricing them, and that he has never once won a haggle against somebody who says nothing.

track.lanes: They say the Genie cannot pass three of a thing without pricing them, and that he has never won a haggle against somebody who says nothing.

after.says: At the crack they say the Genie cannot pass three of a thing without pricing them. Somebody carrying a pie as him has proved it {{n}} time{{s}}: three for the price of two, then two for one, then a coin handed back to nobody in particular. Nobody was selling. He lost anyway.

entries.title: Stopped to smell
entries.note: In the bloom garden they say Mr. BaneWAP has never once stopped to smell a thing he announced.

track.lanes: In the bloom garden they say Mr. BaneWAP has never once stopped to smell a thing he announced.

after.says: In the bloom garden they say Mr. BaneWAP has never once stopped to smell a thing he announced. Somebody carrying a pie has stopped him {{n}} time{{s}}: a thorned rose cleared, his own off switch thrown before it could fade, and he stood smelling it as if it might last.
